text: Fix applied for the non-string (timestamp / js Date / Day.js object) parse path in src/plugin/timezone/index.js; it now matches moment-timezone in the UTC container. Still verifying under the other TZs the suite runs in (Pacific/Auckland, Europe/London, America/Whitehorse).

Investigating: the "Convert format Z" behaviour looks correct in the UTC container, so the bug is likely TZ-dependent (it shows up when the machine's local zone is not UTC, e.g. Pacific/Auckland). Narrowing it down now.
Fix applied and verified against moment-timezone (timestamp / js Date / Day.js object now parse as absolute instants). Running the full suite now to confirm no pre-existing test regressed.

Found it: the offset computed in the tz() conversion was not rounded, so any instance with milliseconds produced a fractional offset (e.g. format('Z') => '-04:0.008333333333325754'). Fixed with Math.round; verifying now.
Fixed src/locale/nl.js ordinal (Dutch ordinals were '1.', '2.'; they must be '1ste', '2de', '8ste', '20ste' like moment's nl locale). Verifying 1-31 and the full suite now.
Investigating src/plugin/weekYear/index.js now (week-year rollover for the previous year is likely missing).

Fixed: src/plugin/timezone/index.js now routes non-string input (timestamp, js Date, Day.js object) through d(input).tz(timezone) instead of parsing it as wall-clock time. Verified against moment-timezone and the full suite (530 passed, no pre-existing test broken).
Fixed: the offset computed in tz() was fractional for instants with milliseconds (format('Z') => '-04:0.008333333333325754'); now rounded with Math.round, matching moment-timezone. Full suite passes.
src/locale/nl.js ordinal updated to the Dutch ordinal rules (1ste, 2de, 8ste, 20ste); still verifying the exact expected strings against moment's nl locale.

Fixed: weekYear() now also returns year - 1 when the month is January and the week of year is >= 52 (e.g. en-gb/zh-cn/fr yearStart:4, 2016-01-01 => 2015). Verified against moment across all locales and dates 2015-2023.
A subagent is fixing the customParseFormat meridiem (AM/PM) locale bug; I will verify and report when it lands.
